identity.name: The Straits Times
identity.description: Singapore's English-language newspaper of record, covering national politics, business and Southeast Asian affairs.

ownership.ownershipNotes: Published by SPH Media Trust, a company limited by guarantee that took over Singapore Press Holdings' media business in 2021. It receives government funding while retaining commercial operations.

editorialOrientation.evidence: Close institutional proximity to Singapore's government and a history of restrained coverage of domestic political opposition; regional reporting is more plural.
editorialOrientation.source: Ownership and self-description via Official about page; secondary references; feed-level sample

politicalLeaning.evidence: MBFC rates Right-Center; pro-establishment, technocratic framing on domestic policy.

economicPerspective.evidence: Coverage is oriented toward Singapore's trade, finance and investment model.

internationalAlignment.evidence: Frames regional affairs through Singapore's trade interests, ASEAN centrality and stable technocratic governance.
internationalAlignment.source: Ownership, editorial positioning and regional coverage sample

reliability.evidence: MBFC credibility High; established newspaper of record, though domestic political coverage is constrained.

externalRatings.notes: MBFC: Right-Center; credibility High; no parsed factual score (retrieved 2026-10-25).

intelligence.knownPerspective: Singapore establishment/technocratic voice. Explains Southeast Asia through trade, investment, ASEAN process and governance stability, with limited adversarial coverage of domestic power.

selectionRationale: Provides a key Southeast Asian establishment perspective and regional business coverage, with explicit state-proximity caveats.

research.researchNotes: Existing production mapping retained, but MBFC suggests Right-Center and ownership is a public-service trust with government funding. Review mapping with schema migration. Research is feed-level only; full article sampling and peer review remain outstanding.
